title: Output consistency audit and signature tests for KV proxy hits
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Background: We have observed cases where cached KV lookups (a.k.a. prefix/KV proxy hits) change the model surface output in ways that are not explainable by request-level non-determinism alone. This ticket creates an automated audit and signature-testing harness that flags semantic deltas introduced by cache hits across config and model updates.

Scope: build a repeatable pipeline that: 1) runs a representative prompt matrix with cache enabled vs cache-disabled; 2) computes lightweight semantic signatures (combination of n-gram overlap, embedding distance, and structured-field equality where applicable); 3) classifies deltas by severity (formatting, token-level noise, content drift, hallucination risk); 4) emits alerts and triage artifacts for PRs that change kernel selection, KV prefetching, prefix eviction, or model binary.

Out of scope: deep manual eval of content quality for low-frequency prompts; full human labelling for every delta (we will sample).
acceptance_criteria:
- Automated job runs on every runtime or model config change and writes a per-change report to S3/drive.
- Signature comparison shows baseline vs candidate with delta buckets (nil/low/medium/high) and counts for each bucket.
- Alerts created for high-severity deltas with links to sample inputs and side-by-side outputs.
- CI gate can be toggled to block release on configurable threshold of high deltas.
- Documentation for how to interpret signatures and how to add new prompt testsets.
test_plan:
1) Assemble a core prompt matrix (500 prompts) covering short completions, multi-turn chat, code synthesis, and structured JSON outputs.
2) Run runs: baseline (cache disabled), candidate (cache enabled), and candidate with cache invalidation.
3) Compute metrics: lexical delta rate, mean embedding distance (sentence-transformer), structured-field equality % for known-format prompts, and policy-tag regressions.
4) Thresholds: flag when >1% of prompts move to 'medium' or any prompt to 'high'.
5) Provide manual review workflow for 'high' samples with links to GH PR and runtime logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (alpha): run nightly audit, store reports, no CI gating. Phase 2 (beta): enable PR annotation and reviewer links for runtime changes. Phase 3 (ga): optional CI block for enterprise branches and protected releases.
mitigation_plan:
- If a high-severity delta is detected, automatically: 1) open a regression ticket and attach failing samples; 2) create a shadow rollback candidate (disable cache or use older kernel selection) for repro; 3) notify on-call runtime team and the owning PR.
- Provide recommended mitigations per delta type (e.g., tighten eviction policy for prefix collisions; disable prefix-prefetch for that model family; force exact-match bypass).
updates: 2026-02-22: Spike completed for embedding-signature approach. Compared SBERT vs in-house cosine; SBERT chosen for speed/consistency.
2026-02-26: Collected initial prompt matrix (n=520) from user-facing flows and internal eval sets; stored in s3://redwood-evals/kv-signature/seed-20260226/.

2026-03-03: Prototype job implemented in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pulls/4371 — harness runs baseline vs cached candidate and outputs CSV + diffs.json (CSV schema is simple rows of prompt_id, baseline_hash, candidate_hash, lexical_delta, embed_distance, severity).
2026-03-08: First-nightly run produced 12 medium deltas and 2 high deltas; both high samples tied to speculative prefetch path introduced in runtime PR #4328.
2026-03-12: Decided with runtime leads to instrument additional KV hit metadata (prefetch_tag, origin_kernel) in telemetry to make triage easier. Added 'prefetch_tag' to report rows.
